# Tiled horizontal advection adoption (#489)

User-authorized runtime integration after the positive benchmark-only screen at `de3d6682` / report `b55285e6`. Base is accepted v4 main `60287e19` (PR #478). Preserve the frozen #481 negative result; this experiment changes field/derivative/flux scheduling and retains inverse-y columns for one active plane per worker, not a full depth volume.

The screen measured 26.5–31.2% horizontal-stage time reductions. It excluded all vertical preparation/projection, phase/assembly, forcing and integration, so whole-model benefit must be measured. First retain the existing MM schedule and physical bundle; no tracer optimization or MATLAB scientific change. Depth<=4 and target-specific buffers limit scratch; cap capacity at the largest worker partition. Memory is a reported trade-off, not a promised reduction. Require credible EddyTide improvement and investigate other model regressions exceeding 3%.

The native operator consumes immutable base spectra, target z spectra (overwritten by flux only after gathering each tile), full u/v/w/eta output, and dLnN2. Actual row/column/reuse counters are collected per worker. All fallible spectral preparation precedes execution. Existing kernel reconstruction supplies spectra without performing or counting a physical inverse, so modal/MM code remains authoritative. Hydro requires one extra H slot; Bouss uses existing slots.

The forcing engine publishes the four ordinary physical nodes atomically using `evaluateGroup`, covering horizontal execution and vertical projection. Only reuse policy and all-empty nodes qualify. Ready/partially ready nodes, low-memory, diagnostics/captures, borrowed fields and unsupported providers retain the existing path. Derived diagnostics keep their own event identity. Failure never publishes the group or accumulates temporary flux. Kernel preparation keeps explicit view/component validity; context teardown invalidates it.

Team: coordinator owns family kernels, runtime, qualification and compute; one reused worker owns provider/operator; one reused reviewer owns bounded runtime tests and independent lifecycle review. No competing builds or timing by agents. Shared guides (caching, package design/release, profiling, documentation), repository AGENTS and optimization workflow were read. No package metadata or versioned snapshots changed.
